editorial_intent: The plate schematizes the multi-target mechanism of botanical polyphenols: electrophilic modification of Keap1 cysteine thiol groups unleashes Nrf2 nuclear translocation to transcribe protective antioxidant enzymes, while simultaneously blocking NF-κB nuclear entry, preserving mitochondrial electron transport, and initiating autophagic SASP debris clearance.
subject: An intricate cross-section of a damaged neuron showing the Nrf2-Keap1 electrophilic sensor switch alongside a double-membrane mitochondrion, where cysteine thiol modifications on Keap1 trigger Nrf2 nuclear entry while NF-κB transcription factor complexes are trapped outside the nuclear envelope.
setting: Subtle background framing featuring stippled SASP interference rings disassembling inside a precision rotary autophagic compass wheel that transitions seamlessly into a clean hexagonal cellular honeycomb motif.
composition: Asymmetric Post-Constructivist dual-axis layout: a vertical nuclear envelope gradient on the right intersecting a horizontal mitochondrial bioenergetic axis on the left, connected by precise geometric vectors of active molecular translocation printed on unbleached archival cotton paper.
